::: {#sol-two-linear}

Substituting the first layer into the second,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\matr{W}_2 \paren{\matr{W}_1 \vx + \vecf{b}_1} + \vecf{b}_2
&= \matr{W}_2 \matr{W}_1 \vx + \matr{W}_2 \vecf{b}_1 + \vecf{b}_2
&& \text{(distribute $\matr{W}_2$)} \\
&= \underbrace{\paren{\matr{W}_2 \matr{W}_1}}_{10 \times 64} \vx
+ \underbrace{\paren{\matr{W}_2 \vecf{b}_1 + \vecf{b}_2}}_{10 \times 1}
&& \text{(group the terms that do not involve $\vx$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

So the stack is an [affine function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/linear-regression.html#def-affine-function) of $\vx$,
the same kind of function as one `nn.Linear(64, 10)`,
with weight matrix $\matr{W}_2 \matr{W}_1$ and bias $\matr{W}_2 \vecf{b}_1 + \vecf{b}_2$.
The 32 numbers in the middle add nothing that one layer could not compute.

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
first = nn.Linear(64, 32)
second = nn.Linear(32, 10)
weight = second.weight @ first.weight
bias = second.weight @ first.bias + second.bias
stacked = second(first(x_test))
one_layer = x_test @ weight.T + bias
stack_gap = (stacked - one_layer).abs().max().item()
print(weight.shape, bias.shape, stack_gap)
```

On the `r py$n_test` test images,
the stack and the single layer agree to within `r format(py$stack_gap, digits = 2)`,
a rounding error.
`nn.Linear` stores $\matr{W}$ with one row per output,
and computes `x @ weight.T + bias` for a [tensor](pytorch-basics.qmd#def-tensor) `x` with one row per image.

:::
